answer: Because the forge index resolves every citation against the mirror checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the nadir audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 110 aliases as a result burns the authoring cost 110 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
